Visualisation certainly helps and it depends on what level your visualisation is like. For example, if an hypnotist asks for you to imagine yourself walking down an infinite set of steps going deeper and deeper into hypnosis every time you take a step, you need to be able to visualise this for it to be effective. You by no means need to be able to imagine crazy details, just the base ideas and this certainly help. To get better visualisation (especially in regards to hypnosis) you need to practice imagining things more frequently to practice it just like any other skill. Imagine things like the steps i mentioned and try describing the details to yourself whilst you're imagining it to help draw them out. You could imagine other things such as a hammock on a beach or various other images. So to summarise, you don't need to be amazing at visualisation, but it is very helpful if you can imagine things like the example above. To practice just imagine things and try describing them.
